Historical-baseline placement: this is the first CFTC administrative
enforcement action against a centralized cryptocurrency exchange in
the dataset, following the 2015-09-17 Coinflip/Derivabit order
(coinflip-cftc-derivabit-2015) which established Bitcoin as a
"commodity" under the CEA but targeted a derivatives-style platform
rather than a spot/margin exchange. The 2016-06-02 Bitfinex order
extends CFTC reach to the spot-exchange margin product surface and
is a structural sibling of the later 2020-10-01 BitMEX CFTC/DOJ
enforcement (bitmex-cftc-doj-2020) at much larger scale. Also

analysis_notes:
comparison documenting the first-ever OFAC sanction of a virtual currency
mixer. Blender.io was designated 94 days before Tornado Cash and tests whether the Tornado
cascade shape generalizes to the mixer class, or whether Tornado's cross-layer reaction was
driven by Tornado-specific properties (Ethereum native, smart-contract-based, USDC-
interacting).

Key structural differences from Tornado 2022:
- Bitcoin-only (no asset_onchain layer, no ETH PBS-relay analogue)
- Pre-Merge (no L1 Ethereum infrastructure existed yet)
- Operator-run mixer service, not a smart-contract protocol
- Centralized domain operator who could physically shut the service down

The one grounded observation is at L4 frontend: blender.io was reduced to a default nginx
landing page within 10 days of designation. This is the cleanest "operator-abandonment"
pattern in the dataset — the Blender operators themselves dismantled the application rather
than fighting or relocating. This contrasts with Sinbad 2023-11 (foreign mixer, domain and
service persistent post-designation) and Tornado 2022 (US-compliance-driven collapse of US-
hosted frontend infrastructure while the underlying Ethereum protocol remained operational
because it could not be turned off).

Follow-up directions (post-admission): (1) chain-analytics firm report (Chainalysis / TRM Labs / Elliptic)
tagging of Blender-clustered BTC addresses, quantifying CEX deposit blocks; (2) any news
or legal archive for the Blender operators' post-2022 fate.

Admitting conservatively as comparison rather than comparison — the dataset's
Bitcoin-only event class currently has no observed_change at L1 / asset / RPC layers because
those layers are structurally not_applicable for Bitcoin. The L4 observed_change alone is
enough to meet comparison's 1-2 changed-layer requirement once the draft is promoted.

This event is the direct cross-temporal sibling of the already-admitted
china-pboc-crypto-ban-2021; the pair should be treated as the
canonical 2013 / 2021 PBOC comparison case in the dataset. The 2013
notice was the first comprehensive PRC central-bank action against
Bitcoin and established the regulatory frame (Bitcoin as virtual
commodity, banks excluded, exchanges treated as internet-information-
service providers under MIIT) that the 2021 nine-ministry joint
notice extended into a full ban on crypto-business activity.

Substantive findings:
- Five-ministry joint notice (PBOC + MIIT + CBRC + CSRC + CIRC).
- Bitcoin classified as a "virtual commodity," not currency.
- Financial institutions and payment service providers prohibited
  from offering Bitcoin-related services (custody / payment /
  conversion / insurance).
- Bitcoin exchanges required to register with MIIT as
  "internet information service providers" and to apply AML
  identification.
- Banks directed to refuse Bitcoin-related accounts.
- Observed cascade: within ~13 days, BTC China (~2013-12-18 CNY
  deposit pause), OKCoin, and Huobi all paused CNY deposit channels
  in compliance.

citation.note:
PBOC original publication of Notice 2013/289 (公告 [2013]289号 /
"Notice on Preventing Bitcoin Risks" / 关于防范比特币风险的通知),
issued 2013-12-05 jointly by five PRC ministries: People's Bank
of China (PBOC), Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
(MIIT), China Banking Regulatory Commission (CBRC), China
Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), and China Insurance
Regulatory Commission (CIRC). Core provisions: (1) classified
Bitcoin as a "virtual commodity" rather than legal-tender
currency; (2) prohibited financial institutions and payment
service providers from buying/selling Bitcoin or providing
Bitcoin-related custody, payment, conversion, or insurance
services; (3) required Bitcoin exchanges to register with MIIT
as "internet information service providers" and to comply with
anti-money-laundering identification rules; (4) directed banks
to refuse Bitcoin-related accounts. The pbc.gov.cn URL path
format has changed since 2013; the provisional wayback
anchor uses Wayback Machine year-prefix lookup and the specific
capture timestamp requires re-pinning during human audit before
this citation may serve as an admission anchor in its own right.
Marked evidence_use=contextual_unarchived pending that re-pin.

State Council (gov.cn) reproduction of the joint five-ministry
announcement of Notice 2013/289 on 2013-12-05. Marked
evidence_use=contextual_unarchived; the live gov.cn URL has
path-format drift since 2013 and the specific Wayback snapshot
timestamp is to be re-pinned during human audit.

US Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor entry titled
"China: Regulators Issue Notice on Bitcoin Risks" dated
2014-01-13, providing an English-language summary of Notice
2013/289 and naming all five issuing PRC ministries. Used
here as a contextual translation anchor; the live loc.gov URL
format is stable and routinely captured by Wayback, but the
specific snapshot timestamp is to be re-pinned during human
audit. Marked evidence_use=contextual_unarchived pending that
re-pin.

timestamp_sources.note:
Notice 2013/289 carries a 2013-12-05 issuance date. The notice
text and all contemporaneous Chinese-language and English-language
secondary coverage agree on the 2013-12-05 publication day.
Day-level precision is appropriate because the PRC ministerial
joint notice does not carry intra-day publication timing in the
public record.

analysis_notes:
**NEW EVENT AUTHORED — DRYRUN 2026-05-16** (promoted from
candidate_triggers/coinbase-irs-john-doe-summons-2016.yaml per the
2026-05-16 staged historical-baseline expansion). Historical-baseline
anchor for the first major US IRS enforcement action against a US-based
centralized crypto exchange. Petition filed 2016-11-17 in the U.S.
District Court for the Northern District of California by the DOJ Tax
Division on behalf of the IRS; court authorization for service entered
2016-11-30 (the DOJ press release).

Trigger-type choice: a John Doe summons authorization is a federal civil
court order, not a criminal indictment or seizure order. trigger.type is
therefore court_civil_order (which maps to S3_doj_sec_cftc_fiod in the
validator's trigger-type-to-stratum map). trigger.actor is recorded as
US_DISTRICT_COURT_ND_CAL_IRS to credit both the issuing court and the
IRS as the substantive petitioning agency; the literal string "US_DOJ"
is deliberately avoided in the actor field because the validator's
actor/type-coherence rule reserves the US_DOJ actor for trigger.type ∈
{doj_indictment, doj_seizure_order}. The DOJ Tax Division's role as
the filing prosecutor on behalf of the IRS is noted in the press-release
citation but not in the actor literal.

Empirical shape: comparison. The cascade has exactly one observed_change
layer (offramp_cex: Coinbase's published petition-opposition disclosure
one day after the 2016-11-17 petition filing). L0/L1/L3 are not
applicable to a tax-records summons; L4 frontend is not_measured rather
than not_applicable because a future Wayback diff of coinbase.com across
the 2016-11–2018-02 summons-and-narrowed-order window could in principle
promote it. asset_onchain is not_applicable (Bitcoin has no issuer
admin-freeze surface). admission_tier is empirical_case (≥1
strong-attribution observed_change layer; Coinbase's blog post names
the petition directly).

Subsequent procedural history (referenced for context, not as separately
retained observations): on 2017-11-28 the N.D. Cal. court issued a
narrowed production order requiring Coinbase to produce records for
approximately 14,000 customers with $20,000+ transactions during
2013–2015 (significantly narrower than the original all-US-customers
scope); Coinbase notified affected customers in early 2018 and produced
records to the IRS in 2018. The 2017-11-29 Coinbase blog post
("Coinbase Obtains Partial Victory Over IRS") describes the narrowed
order, but the available Wayback snapshots return Medium identity-flow
302 redirects rather than the article body, so the narrowed-order
state change is not retained here as an independently archived
observation. A future audit pass could attempt a new Wayback save of
the medium.com mirror or supplement with the underlying court order
(N.D. Cal. case 17-CV-1431-JSC).

Related events: sec-v-coinbase-2023 (structural sibling: federal civil
enforcement against Coinbase as named target entity, eight years later
and on securities-law theory rather than tax-records theory),
nydfs-bitlicense-2015-06 (structural sibling: pre-2017 state/federal
US regulatory pressure on US crypto exchanges, also retained as
historical-baseline temporal-tier evidence), and
silk-road-doj-seizure-2013 (earliest 2013–2016 DOJ-stratum
historical-baseline event; uses the same Wayback-anchor + live-stub
citation pattern for justice.gov press releases).

coverage.note:
A John Doe summons is a tax-records production order, not an ISP-level
reachability block. Standard public-web L0 instruments (Censored
Planet, OONI) do not apply to a tax-records summons.

Bitcoin, pre-Merge by ~5.5 years; consensus-layer filtering surfaces
tracked by this dataset (PBS relays, mev-watch / censorship.pics) did
not exist in 2016 and are not implicated by a tax-records summons in
any case.

Hosted-RPC providers (Infura, Alchemy, QuickNode) did not yet operate
at meaningful scale in 2016, and a tax-records summons is not an
RPC-mediated transaction-rejection surface. Out of scope.

No Coinbase.com frontend takedown or domain-state change is implicated
by the IRS John Doe summons. A retained L4 null claim would require a
Wayback/frontend artifact across the 2016-11–2018-02 summons window;
until that denominator is captured, this remains unmeasured rather
than not_applicable.

Bitcoin has no issuer admin-freeze surface, and the John Doe summons
did not invoke any on-chain freeze or seizure mechanism. Out of scope.

Coinbase as a US-regulated centralized exchange is the directly named
target of the John Doe summons. The measurable platform-side state
change is Coinbase's published opposition stance, captured on
2016-11-18 via the company blog: Coinbase publicly committed to
oppose the petition in court, marking the first time a major US
crypto exchange publicly disclosed an IRS tax-enforcement-records
summons against itself. The observation is scoped to the
petition-opposition disclosure as captured on Wayback within one day
of the petition filing; it does not encode the subsequent 2017-11-28
narrowed production order, which is referenced in analysis_notes but
not separately measured here for lack of an admission-grade primary
capture.

This event is the canonical historical-baseline anchor for the
CFTC-against-crypto-operator analysis thread in the dataset.
Substantive significance:

1. **First CFTC enforcement action against a cryptocurrency

   crypto enforcement action by roughly a year and the
   cftc-v-ooki-dao-2022 DAO-as-legal-person enforcement by ~7 years.
2. **Commodity classification of Bitcoin under the CEA.** The order
   formally establishes that "Bitcoin and other virtual currencies"

   observable cascade shape: the regulator does not seize the
   domain (contrast btc-e-doj-2017 DOJ domain seizure), and the
   compliance response is operator-side cessation of the offering.

via usdtbanlist.com reveals they were **already blocked by Tether on 2025-04-30 — ~188
days BEFORE the OFAC designation**. This reverses the expected cross-layer causation
direction: rather than "OFAC → Tether freeze cascade," the observed pattern is "Tether
freeze precedes OFAC action by 6 months," suggesting either (a) upstream Treasury /
FBI / TRM Labs intelligence reaches Tether months before formal SDN publication, or

tagging) independently of the formal OFAC process. This is a paper-worthy structural
finding: **the timing direction of the asset-layer cascade is opposite to what the
dataset's comparison class presumes**.

verification would cross-reference Tronscan logs for each of the 53 addresses to
confirm whether the 2025-04-30 batch-freeze covered all of them.

analysis_notes:
comparison documenting the 2025-08-14 OFAC designation of the Grinex / Old
Vector / A7 Russian virtual-currency network, framed by Treasury as the operational
successor to Garantex (originally designated 2022-04-05; see garantex-ofac-2022).

The most notable empirical observation is at L1 consensus: a sharp step in aggregate
censoring-relay share from 0% to 86% three days after the event (2025-08-17), settling to
the 38-42% range by early September. The shape is unusual — unlike prior events where L1
responses were either null (single-wallet designations) or gradual post-PBS ramps
(tornado-cash-ofac-2022). A step-up of this magnitude is most plausibly explained by a
relay-ecosystem composition change (a single large-share relay flipping policy) rather than
a direct Grinex-address-driven filter update; pending per-relay data, attribution is
marked unknown.

Follow-up directions (post-admission): (1) per-relay decomposition of the 2025-08-17 step to determine which
relays drove it and whether their block-filter lists added the Grinex 8 ETH addresses;
(2) Tronscan queries for USDT-TRC20 freeze transactions on the 11 TRX addresses (high
probability of fresh freezes given Tether's typical response time); (3) pinned
chain-analytics firm report tagging the Grinex cluster.

Classifying as comparison per its relationship to the Garantex 2022 original
designation; the two events together test whether successor-entity designations reproduce
the original cascade shape. Early read: asset / CEX reactions are expected to mirror the
original (per Tether behaviour), but the L1 shape is materially different in 2025 than in
2022 because of the post-Merge relay-ecosystem evolution.

analysis_notes:
comparison documenting India's 2018-04-06 RBI Circular prohibiting banks
from servicing crypto entities — the first major nation-state banking-level crypto ban
in a major economy (cf. China PBOC 2021, Nigeria CBN 2021, Turkey CBRT 2021). Structurally
distinct from OFAC designations: no address set, no individual target, no digital-
currency address enumeration — instead, an industry-class banking severance.

This is a sibling event to china-pboc-crypto-ban-2021 (admitted). Both share the
comparison shape: nation-state regulator cuts banking rails rather than targeting
specific crypto addresses. The RBI ban was overturned by the Supreme Court 2020-03-04,
making it the only ban in the dataset with a legally-forced reversal — that would be a
natural comparison candidate for future addition.

coverage.note: Banking-channel ban, not a DNS / connectivity action.

Indian exchange frontends (zebpay.com, unocoin.com, wazirx.com, etc.) remained
accessible; the ban operated at the INR-deposit/withdrawal banking layer rather than
at the L4 application layer. Wayback bracketing could document continued frontend
availability but that's less informative than the off-ramp impact.

The RBI circular is by construction an off-ramp-layer event — it severed banking
rails between Indian exchanges and INR. Zebpay, then India's largest exchange, cited
the RBI circular as the reason for shutting down its Indian operations in September
2018. Attached as observed_change with direct attribution (the circular itself names
the banking-service severance as the regulatory mandate).

sources.note:
The RBI circular text itself is the legal instrument mandating the banking
cut-off. It gives a 3-month compliance deadline from issuance (2018-04-06), so
effective-observation timestamp is 2018-07-06. attribution=direct because the
circular specifies the regulatory mandate and timing.

or relocated as a direct consequence."

target.enumeration_note:

and the broader class of Indian crypto businesses that relied on INR bank rails. Target
treated as entity-level at the population level.

citation.note:
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Circular DBR.No.BP.BC.104/08.13.102/2017-18 dated
2018-04-06 titled "Prohibition on dealing in Virtual Currencies (VCs)". Directed
all RBI-regulated entities (including scheduled commercial banks, cooperative banks,
NBFCs, and payment system operators) to cease providing services to any individual
or business dealing with or settling virtual currencies, and to exit existing
relationships within three months. Effectively cut off Indian bank access for
crypto exchanges from 2018-07-06 onward. Overturned by Supreme Court of India on
2020-03-04 in Internet and Mobile Association of India v. RBI — that Supreme Court
ruling is a separate event (candidate for future addition as a comparison
showing ban-reversal).

comparison documenting South Korea's 2022-03-25 Travel Rule
effective-date. First and one of the strictest national Travel Rule
implementations globally — KRW 1M threshold is an order of magnitude
lower than typical international implementations. Structural
contribution to the dataset: a non-OFAC, non-sanction, regulatory-KYC
event that nonetheless materially affects crypto-transfer flows.
Paper-worthy because it illustrates censorship-measurement questions
at the metadata layer (transfer-approval gating) rather than the
asset- or list-layer.

coverage.note: Travel Rule is backend KYC/transaction-metadata enforcement, not frontend takedown.
No asset-layer blacklist; the rule restricts transfer metadata, not the underlying asset.

sources.note:
KR FSC is the primary legal actor for Travel Rule enforcement.
Effective 2022-03-25; immediate application to all registered
Korean VASPs (Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, Korbit, etc.). All crypto
transfers ≥KRW 1M must carry originator/beneficiary KYC data.
Direct attribution: the FSC rule itself mandates the behavior.

Second anchor to same FSC index; FATF Recommendation 16 framework
context. Cross-reference to Specific Financial Transactions
Reporting Act (특정금융정보법) implementing regulations.

scoped_claim:

transmission requirements on all registered Korean VASPs for crypto
transfers ≥KRW 1M, representing the first national-scale FATF
Recommendation 16 implementation in the dataset and the strictest
threshold globally. Paper-relevant as a metadata-layer censorship-
adjacent regulatory event distinct from OFAC / sanction modes."

disable its website and mobile applications for Malaysian users.
Sibling case in the 2021 multi-jurisdictional Binance regulator wave:
UK FCA 2021-06-26, Netherlands DNB 2021-08-18, Singapore MAS
2021-09-02. Binance had already been on the SC's Investor Alert List

Paper-relevant contrast vs UK FCA (uk-fca-binance-markets-2021): the
SC action is a direct frontend-disable order (website + mobile apps
for Malaysian users) whose primary observational axis is L4 frontend,
whereas the FCA action was a single-entity (BML) registration notice
whose load-bearing observational axis was offramp_cex via the UK
retail-bank payment-rail cascade (Barclays / Santander). Both are S4
nation-state actions; both are empirical_case shape=comparison; the
Malaysia case foregrounds the regulator-directed operator-compliance
frontend channel that the FCA case lacks.

the SC order is harder-edged (explicit disable directive with a
compliance deadline) than the DNB warning (Wwft-registration warning

timeline is compressed (disable within 14 business days of 2021-07-30)
vs the DNB slow-cascade (warning 2021-08 → fine 2022-04 → exit
2022-07).

comparison documenting Nigeria's 2021-02-05 CBN ban on bank-crypto
facilitation. Third major nation-state banking cut-off in the dataset (after India 2018,
China 2021). Notable context: Nigeria had the highest per-capita crypto adoption in
Africa going into this ban; the subsequent P2P substitution pattern is a natural
experiment for how crypto networks route around banking severance.

coverage.note:
CBN circular directly severed Naira deposit/withdrawal channels for cryptocurrency
exchanges. Subsequent market reaction: Nigeria rapidly became the global leader in
P2P Bitcoin trading (peer-to-peer crypto networks substituted for banking rails),
per Chainalysis / Usefultulips data; counterpart CEXes (Binance, Paxful) adapted
with P2P marketplace features. Attached as observed_change with direct attribution
(the CBN letter text itself is the regulatory mandate).

sources.note:
CBN circular is the legal instrument. attribution=direct because the letter
explicitly mandates the banking cut-off.

of Dealings in Cryptocurrencies or Facilitation of Payments for Cryptocurrency
Exchanges." Directed all banks and financial institutions in Nigeria to close

analysis_notes:
**NEW EVENT AUTHORED — DRYRUN 2026-05-16** (Phase 2 of the 2026-05-16
staged-release plan): historical-baseline anchor for the 2015-06-24
NYDFS BitLicense final rule and the ShapeShift / Kraken / Bitfinex /
Poloniex NY-exit cascade. Per Agent B M2 finding, this event had no
candidate-ledger entry because the us_state_regulator_archives source
frame did not exist until Phase 1 of 2026-05-16. Origin is
human_reviewed because the YAML was drafted directly by the maintainer
workflow (not generated by an agent_draft watcher), and the captures
in sources/http_captures/nydfs-bitlicense-2015-06/ are real Wayback
pulls retrieved 2026-05-16. For a real release this DRYRUN marker
would be replaced by the production-promotion stamp after an
additional independent human audit.

Trigger-type choice: NYDFS is a US sub-national (state) financial
regulator, and the BitLicense is an administrative rule-making, not a
criminal or civil enforcement action. The schema 0.2.0 trigger.type
vocabulary does not include a state_regulator_action enum value, and
Phase 1 (us_state_regulator_archives source frame) maps to research
stratum S3 by convention. The least-bad existing enum is
court_civil_order (which already maps to S3_doj_sec_cftc_fiod in the
validator's trigger-type-to-stratum map), used here to represent a
state administrative-regulatory order with binding legal effect.
trigger.actor=US_NYDFS does not match any of the actor-coherence
patterns (US_SEC / US_CFTC / US_FINCEN / US_DOJ / US_OFAC /
EU_COUNCIL), so no actor/type-coherence conflict is raised. Adding a
proper state_regulator_action trigger-type enum is left as a future
schema improvement (see Phase 3 candidate-ledger discussion).

Empirical shape: comparison. The cascade is L4-only: four named
exchanges (ShapeShift, Kraken, Bitfinex, Poloniex) exited NY between
2015-06-25 and 2015-09-08. Only one distinct layer (l4_frontend) shows
observed_change, so empirical_shape=comparison rather than cascade,
even though four separate operators are affected. Admission tier is
empirical_case (≥1 strong-attribution observed_change layer; Kraken
and ShapeShift carry attribution=direct).

Related events: coinbase-india-exit-2022 (structural sibling:
exchange market-exit responding to regulator informal/formal pressure)
and india-rbi-crypto-ban-2018 (structural sibling: nation-state-level
regulatory severance of crypto market access). The BitLicense is the
earliest clean L4-frontend regulatory-cascade case in the dataset.

coverage.note:
The BitLicense is a state-licensing regime, not a network-level
block. ISP reachability of NY users to the named operators was not
altered by the regulation; the operators themselves geo-fenced or

Exchanger." Announced jointly with the US Attorney's Office for
the Northern District of California. Core terms: (1) $700,000
civil monetary penalty assessed by FinCEN against Ripple Labs
Inc. and its wholly-owned subsidiary XRP II, LLC for willful
violations of the Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), including (a) acting

a separate non-prosecution agreement (NPA) with the US Attorney's
Office N.D. Cal. resolving the criminal investigation, conditioned
on the FinCEN settlement and on Ripple's adoption of the
compliance undertakings. This is the FIRST civil enforcement
action by FinCEN against a virtual-currency exchanger and a
canonical historical-baseline anchor for the
FinCEN-as-virtual-currency-regulator posture established under
the 2013-03-18 FinCEN guidance (FIN-2013-G001).

- The asset-layer cascade has a separate corporate-compliance clock. Circle tends to
  act within days of OFAC designation; Tether historically acted slower or not at all,
  then executed retroactive batches.
- The 2023-12-09 batch likely reflects a specific Tether policy change or external
  trigger (possibly the US Attorney's Office announcement of criminal charges against
  Tether operators ~Nov 2023, or internal compliance escalation). Needs further
  research.
- This event class is **non-OFAC-triggered** (stratum S5) — it is an issuer action
  NOT tied to a single OFAC designation date, but to a Tether internal decision.

frozen by Tether on 2023-12-09 04:30-06:00 UTC via Etherscan log query of USDT

Reverse-cascade pilot with direct operator attribution on two of six
layers. The trigger is the 2025-03-21 OFAC delisting. At the asset layer,
a concrete on-chain USDC unblacklist transaction for one target address
lands on 2025-03-22 (primary_onchain, direct). At the frontend layer, the

comment "Instances frozen due to sanctions" is removed from

that the prior code state was a sanctions response; this upgrades L4
attribution from plausible to direct. Official Tornado Cash docs
current-state capture bundle confirms that the UI remains reachable. L0 and
off-ramp rollback remain in coverage rather than observations. The event
stays a cascade by layer count (three changed layers), while only some layers
have direct attribution.

on 3 layers: L1 consensus censoring-relay share dropped ≈25pp within 14

frontend access/listing partially reemerged via maintained UI paths while

reported as n=1 and used to show asymmetry: removal from a sanctions list did

analysis_notes:
comparison documenting the 2022-11-08 OFAC redesignation of Tornado Cash under
DPRK-related authorities (simultaneously removing the original 2022-08-08 Cyber-related
designation). The event expands the Tornado SDN footprint from 38 to 98 addresses (60 net-new)
but occurs against a background in which the full cross-layer cascade had already been triggered
by the 2022-08-08 designation. As a result, the comparison this event anchors is not
"cascade-yes vs cascade-no" but rather "does SDN-list expansion, absent a change in legal
authority's scope, trigger an additional round of layer reactions?"

The one empirically-grounded observation so far is at L1 consensus: Wahrstätter's
relay-censorship data shows that OFAC-compliant relay share was already on a strong rising
trajectory pre-event and plateaued near 73% before and through Nov 8, with no step change
attributable to the redesignation itself. This is a paper-worthy null result — it is the kind
of finding that the dataset's comparison class is designed to surface.

Follow-up directions (post-admission): (1) per-address Etherscan query for the 60 net-new ETH addresses to test
whether Circle issued fresh USDC blacklist transactions on or after 2022-11-08 (drives the
asset_onchain observation shape); (2) a pinned snapshot of MEV-Blocker / OFAC-compliant RPC
filter lists bracketing 2022-11-08 (enables an RPC-layer observation); (3) archival search for
exchange or off-ramp policy statements explicitly referencing the Nov 8 redesignation.

Admitted 2026-04-22 on the basis of the L1 null plus the 1/92 asset_onchain finding (Tether
froze one of the 92 Tornado pool addresses during the 2023-12-09 retroactive sweep — a
structural asymmetry finding relative to individual-wallet designations). RPC / off-ramp
layers remain scoped for follow-up.
